request: What impact did passing Obamacare have on the federal budget?

reply.reply: The enactment-era CBO score projected that the ACA together with related legislation would reduce federal deficits by **$143 billion over 2010–2019**—not that this amount was later confirmed as the actual outcome (CRS R41125, PDF p. 4). The estimate comprised $124 billion in health-care expenditure reductions and revenue, plus $19 billion in education spending reductions (CRS R41125, PDF p. 4). A later baseline projected a $210 billion deficit reduction over FY2012–FY2021 (CRS R41664, PDF p. 7). These are historical projections, not measurements of the law’s realized budget impact; the newest source verified here is from 2012. Details and evidence are in the [brief](output/briefs/case-20261025-153404-f7fc.html).
reply.reasoning: Verified evidence addresses enactment-era and subsequent projected budget effects, but not actual realized impact; the available verified sources are historical.
